sso.samlAttributeHelp: Name or FriendlyName of the attribute in the assertion (e.g. email, mail or http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress). The email is only displayed, never used for matching.

sso.samlTestOk: SAML test sign-in successful: IdP metadata, signature and ACS URL match.
sso.testMissingAttributes: These attributes were missing from the assertion: {claims}

sso.samlAllowUnspecifiedWarning: Caution: a NameID in format unspecified is often a changeable value such as the user name. If the IdP reassigns it, the new person signs in with the linked account. Only enable this if the IdP cannot provide a persistent NameID and never reassigns the identifier.
sso.identityResetWarning: Caution: issuer or IdP metadata changed. If the OIDC issuer, the SAML metadata source or the IdP entity ID or signing certificate changes, saving deletes the existing SSO links of this page for that protocol; users have to link again in their profile.

helpTooltips.saveError: Could not save the help setting. It only applies until the page is reloaded.

newComponent.what: Opens an empty form for a new component on the currently selected status page.
newComponent.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. The new component starts as “Operational”, appears on the public status page right away and can be selected for incidents, maintenance windows and in the subscribe wizard.
newComponent.example: Add a new service “Status API” so you can mark it as affected during the next outage.

newGroup.what: Opens an empty form for a new group on the currently selected status page.
newGroup.effect: A group bundles components and has no status of its own: it always shows the worst status of its members. A group can only be deleted when it is empty.
newGroup.example: Create a group “Core services” and then place the web app and the API in it.

name.what: The display name of the service or system. Required.
name.effect: The name is shown on the public status page, in the subscribe wizard, in the component selection for incidents and maintenance, and in notifications. Changes apply everywhere immediately.

tags.what: Assigns tags to the component, such as countries or regions. Multiple choice; with nothing selected it has no tag.
tags.effect: Visitors of the public status page can filter by these tags. Tags also limit administration: users who have tags assigned may only edit and delete components that share a tag with them or carry the “global” tag. Components without tags can be managed by anyone with write access to this page.
tags.example: Set the tag “DE”: visitors filtering by “DE” see the component, and an editor who only has “US” assigned can no longer change it.

description.what: Optional short text describing what the component covers.
description.effect: Shown below the name on the public status page; the search there also matches words from the description.

status.what: The operating state you set yourself: Operational, Degraded Performance, Partial Outage or Major Outage.
status.effect: Applies to the public status page once you save. If an open incident is assigned to this component, the page shows at least “Degraded Performance”; the worse value wins. Subscribers are not notified by a status change alone; create an incident for that.
status.example: The database responds slowly: choose “Degraded Performance”. Once it runs normally again, switch back to “Operational”.

save.effect: Creates the component or applies your changes. They take effect on the public status page immediately and are recorded in the audit log. Nothing is saved without a name.

cancel.effect: Unsaved input is discarded; the component stays as it was.
cancel.example: Clicked “Edit” by mistake: “Cancel” takes you back to the list without changes.

quickStatus.what: Changes the status directly in the table without opening the form.
quickStatus.effect: Saved immediately on selection, without confirmation, and shown on the public status page and in the audit log right away. Subscribers are not notified.
quickStatus.example: The payments API is partly down: choose “Partial Outage” in its row.

rowActions.what: The “…” menu in the row offers “Edit” (opens the component in the form), “Translations” and “Delete” (after a confirmation).
rowActions.effect: Deleted components disappear from the public status page; this cannot be undone in the interface. Incidents remain but lose their link to it. Both only work if your tags match the component (see “Tags”).
rowActions.example: Delete a retired service “Old customer portal” instead of showing it as an outage forever.

visible.what: Switch “Show on the status page”: decides whether visitors see the component (for a group, including its members).
visible.effect: Switched off, it disappears from the public status page, the availability view, the subscribe wizard and the public overall status. In the admin it stays visible with the “Not public” marker, and status webhooks and status changes keep working. Incidents no longer name it publicly.
visible.example: Hide an internal component “Batch worker” whose status only the team should see in the admin.

slug.what: The identifier of the component (or group): a short, stable key of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 60 characters.
slug.effect: Integrations and the API can address the component with it. It is unique per status page and cannot be changed after creation so existing integrations do not break. Left empty, it is generated from the name (umlauts spelled out, “-2”, “-3” … on duplicates).

group.what: The group the component belongs to in the list and on the status page.
group.effect: Groups bundle components and show the worst status of their children. Saving moves the component; “No group” puts it at the top level.
group.example: Put “Payments API” into the group “Core services”.

search.what: Filters the list by name, description and tag.
search.effect: Only the view changes, nothing is saved. Results appear together with their groups, even when those are collapsed.
search.example: Type “EU” to see all components with the tag “EU”.

importSource.what: The external source you adopt components from.
importSource.effect: Its current components then appear for selection. Nothing changes until you choose “Adopt”.

importSearch.what: Filters the component list by name or group name.
importSearch.effect: Only affects the view. Components you already selected stay selected even when hidden.
importSearch.example: “Postgres” shows all components with that name or in that group.

importList.what: The external components and groups you want to adopt. Multiple selection.
importList.effect: Each selected component becomes an own component with its name, linked to it. A whole group is created as a group with its current components; the group itself is not linked, its status follows its children. Already linked components cannot be selected.
importList.example: Select “Whole group” Database to create the group and all database components at once.

importSelectAll.what: Selects all currently visible components that are not linked yet.
importSelectAll.effect: Only changes the selection, nothing is created. At most 200 components are allowed per run.
importSelectAll.example: Search for “Compute” first, then select all visible.

importClear.effect: Only changes the selection, nothing is created.
importClear.example: Start over after a wrong multiple selection.

importTarget.what: The own group under which the new components are created.
importTarget.effect: “Top level” creates them without a group. New components are appended to the target group and start as “Operational”.
importTarget.example: Choose group “Cloud” so all new components end up there.

importTags.what: Tags given to all newly created components (and groups). Optional.
importTags.effect: As with every component, the tags control who may edit them.
importTags.example: “EU” for components of a European region.

importSubmit.what: Creates components for the selected items and links them.
importSubmit.effect: Everything happens in one step: on an error nothing is created. Already linked and vanished components are skipped and listed afterwards; a second click does not create anything twice.
importSubmit.example: Select 12 components and click “Adopt” to get 12 linked components.

newSource.what: Opens an empty form for a new external status page.
newSource.effect: Nothing is created until you click “Save”. Afterwards the server polls the page at the configured interval and creates its components.
newSource.example: Add your cloud provider's status page to take its incidents into account on your page.

name.what: Display name of the source. Required.
name.effect: The name appears in this list, on mirrored reports, in subscriber notifications and in the outage email.

baseUrl.what: Address of the third-party status page. Required, https only.
baseUrl.effect: The server queries the Summary API v2 at this address. It rejects private, local and internal addresses. A changed address resets the fetch markers.

interval.what: How often the source is polled, in seconds (60 to 86400).
interval.effect: Shorter intervals show incidents sooner but put more load on the third-party page. The value applies from the next fetch.

outageAfter.what: Time in minutes (10 to 1440) without a successful fetch after which the source counts as down.
outageAfter.effect: From then on an admin notice appears, admins receive an email (once, a reminder after 24 hours and an all-clear), and the stale status of the source no longer counts. A single error does not trigger anything.
outageAfter.example: 60: after one hour without success the source counts as down.

active.what: Switches regular polling of the source on or off.
active.effect: Inactive sources are not polled; their links and mirrored reports no longer count. The data is kept.
active.example: Switch off while the provider moves its status page.

save.effect: The input is validated (address, value ranges). The configuration applies immediately; a new source is fetched for the first time at the next tick or with “Fetch now”.
save.example: Fill in the form and click “Save”.

cancel.effect: Input in the form is lost, nothing is saved.
cancel.example: Cancel after a typo in the address and start over.

rowActions.what: Opens the source menu: fetch now, edit or delete.
rowActions.effect: “Fetch now” queries the third-party page immediately and shows the result. “Delete” removes the source with its components, links and mirrored reports.
rowActions.example: After correcting the address choose “Fetch now” to test the connection.

linkComponent.what: The own component whose status should be influenced by the external component. Required.
linkComponent.effect: The effective status of the component is the worst of its own status and that of the linked components. Pure groups cannot be linked, only their components.

linkSource.what: Chooses the source the external component comes from.
linkSource.effect: Only after choosing is the component list of the source loaded and offered in the “External component” field.

linkSearch.what: Filters the component list by name or group name.
linkSearch.effect: Only affects the selection below and changes no data.
linkSearch.example: “Postgres” shows all components with that name or in that group.

linkExternal.what: The external component or whole external group you link. Required.
linkExternal.effect: For a group the worst of its current members counts; new members join automatically, vanished ones do not count.
linkExternal.example: “Whole group: Database” for all database components of a provider.

linkAdd.what: Creates the link between the own component and the external component.
linkAdd.effect: The link applies immediately to the effective status on the status page and to mirrored reports that affect this component. An existing link stays unchanged.
linkAdd.example: Link the component “Database” with the group “Database”.

unlink.what: Removes the link between the own component and the external component.
unlink.effect: The external status no longer colours the component; mirrored reports for this component disappear from the list unless another linked component is affected.
unlink.example: Remove a link set by mistake.

filterKind.what: Shows only incidents or only maintenances.
filterKind.effect: Only changes what this list shows, not the data.
filterKind.example: “Maintenance” to see planned work by providers.

filterState.what: Shows only open or only closed reports.
filterState.effect: Closed reports are shown for the last 30 days only. Only changes the display.

filterSource.what: Shows only reports of one source.
filterSource.effect: Only changes what this list shows.
